Thanks for the quick note. Short answers up front: our recommended pilot structure is a 6–9 month private-offer with monthly metered billing via AWS Marketplace (helps avoid early commitment while enabling co-sell). We can also support a single annual invoice if Procurement needs it — that requires a PO and the Marketplace private-offer to be configured for "seller invoice" activation (adds ~7 business days for activation).

SOC2 report attached (summary). I copied Ben — he’ll pull together a one-pager tailored for buyer approvers with clear decision points.

- Pricing: $0.12 / inference-unit with a 20% pilot discount for the first 90 days, then back to baseline (pilot discount communicated to buyer approvers as a time-limited incentive)
- Billing cadence: Monthly via Marketplace (preferred). If TerraScale needs annual invoicing, we’ll enable seller-invoice on the PO and coordinate with AWS billing to confirm timelines.

Hi Neha/Ben —

We reviewed the summary. TerraScale prefers a 12-month maximum exposure but is open to 9 months. Procurement has two gating requirements before buyer approvers will sign-off:

1) A clear activation timeline for seller-invoice if we opt for annual billing (we need activation < 10 business days post-PO).
2) A buyer-approval matrix showing who at TerraScale signs at what dollar thresholds (we'll supply the matrix if Redwood confirms support for staged activation).

Please provide the activation flow for seller-invoice private-offers and confirm Redwood can stage the offer so that approvals can be routed by threshold. Also, we need the draft private-offer term sheet in Word for our legal team to redline.

Regards,

Team —

Draft term sheet attached (Word). Important internal notes for negotiation:
- Liability cap: standard Redwood clause (1x annual committed fees for pilots) — be prepared to negotiate if customer insists on higher cap.
- Term length: we recommend 9 months for the pilot to preserve flexibility; if Procurement insists on 12 months, ask for an early-termination credit tied to unused committed spend.
- Billing: confirm whether TerraScale will request seller-invoice. If yes, legal will include language requiring PO and specify activation timeline and AWS marketplace seller-invoice dependencies.

Ben: I flagged section 4.3 (billing activation) — I recommend we propose 7 business-day activation SLA for seller-invoice, with an exception clause for AWS processing delays.

Vivek: please prepare a short ops runbook showing the steps we take after PO receipt (onboarding, co-sell enablement, support contact, activation windows). Keep it 1 page for buyer approvers.

Thanks,

Hi Alicia / Procurement team —

Attaching a one-page ops runbook and the activation checklist. TL;DR: if TerraScale wants annual invoicing, the sequence is: PO issued -> Redwood configures private-offer with seller-invoice -> AWS processes seller-invoice activation (~3–7 business days typical) -> we confirm activation and invoice schedule -> TerraScale payables issues first invoice per PO terms. If you keep monthly Marketplace billing, activation is immediate upon private-offer acceptance.

Buyer approval routing: we support staged approvals by dollar thresholds using the Private Offer metadata fields; please send your approver matrix and we’ll map it to the offer.

Next actions:
- Alicia: confirm prefer 9 vs 12 months and whether you need annual invoice.
- Procurement: send approver matrix and preferred PO cadence.
- Neha/Ben: once Alicia confirms, we’ll upload the Word term sheet to DocuSign and send the marketplace private-offer link.

Thanks,
Vivek
